question: Yesterday an engineer used your agent in a named session to map a legacy billing module with Read, Grep, and Glob. Overnight, a teammate merged a refactor that split and renamed most of the files that the agent had read. The engineer will start a new session with a structured summary instead of resuming the old one. What should the summary include to make the new session most reliable?

options.text: Include only the original task request, so the agent rebuilds its understanding of the billing module with no prior findings.
options.reason: This drops the prior findings that are still valid and forces a full re-exploration, while the guide prefers injecting a summary and doing targeted re-analysis.

options.text: Include the conclusions that still hold and a list of the refactored files that the agent must read again before it relies on them.
options.reason: A structured summary keeps the valid findings without the stale tool results and points the agent to the changed files for targeted re-analysis, which is why starting fresh is more reliable.

options.text: Include yesterday's conclusions about every file as current facts, so the agent does not spend tokens reading the refactored files again.
options.reason: Conclusions about the refactored files come from stale tool results, so presenting them as current facts lets the agent reason from outdated information.

options.text: Include the full transcript of yesterday's session with every Read and Grep output, so the agent has the original contents of each file.
options.reason: This puts the stale tool results back into the new context, which removes the advantage that a fresh session with a summary has over resuming with stale tool results.
